From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:

# Project Kestrel: Buyer-Side Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Baseline:** 100% of Paperbark Analytics. AUD 24,000,000. Debt-free/cash-free. NSW law.

**Overall view:** The covering note calls this package "fair and balanced". It is not. In several places the Seller Update describes items as "addressed" or "settled" when the Seller's own Disclosure Letter says otherwise:

- Bluefen consent: not delivered.
- Riverlark facility: not repaid.
- Ironquay: AUD 180,000 still open and no assignment.
- DD-006 incident: still preliminary.

On top of that, the limitation architecture would wrap every claim, including fraud and title, inside a single AUD 4.8m, 18-month regime. We should reject that architecture before negotiating individual numbers.

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap (cl 12.1)
- **Seller:** Aggregate cap for general Warranty Claims of 20% of price (AUD 4,800,000).
- **Buyer wants:** A higher cap, around 40–50% (AUD 9.6m–12m) if there is no W&I policy. The cap must apply only to general Warranty Claims. Fundamental/title, tax, specific indemnities, covenants, leakage and fraud should sit outside it.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 50%, with fallback to around 35% only if the carve-outs are secured. **Reason:** 20% is thin given the known risk items (Bluefen ~30% of revenue, privacy incident, Ironquay IP), and the real value of the cap depends on what sits outside it.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket (cl 12.2)
- **Seller:** De minimis of AUD 25,000 (0.1%). Basket of AUD 250,000 (~1.04%), operating as a deductible, so only the excess is recoverable.
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis of AUD 10,000. A tipping basket of around AUD 120,000 (0.5%), so that once it is exceeded the whole amount is recoverable from the first dollar. Related claims arising from the same facts should aggregate for de minimis purposes. Neither threshold should apply to specific indemnities, tax, title or fraud.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the deductible and accept only a tipping basket. **Reason:** A deductible permanently costs the Buyer AUD 250k. Without aggregation, the de minimis lets the Seller split related losses (see the Sandbar pattern) below the threshold.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit (cl 12.3/13)
- **Seller:** 18 months for general claims. Any limitation applies to all Claims "unless expressly stated otherwise".
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months for general warranties, covering two full audit cycles. Separate, longer periods for tax, title/fundamental and indemnities. The default rule should be reversed: limitations apply only to the categories expressly named.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 24 months and reverse the default. **Reason:** The "unless expressly stated" drafting silently imports 18 months into tax, title and indemnity claims.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same cap and time limit "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** Fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority, share capital, solvency) capped at 100% of price (AUD 24m). Time limit of 6–7 years, matching the NSW limitation period for contract claims. No de minimis or basket. No disclosure against them.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. **Reason:** If title fails, the Buyer has paid AUD 24m for nothing. A AUD 4.8m, 18-month remedy is not a remedy, and "administrative simplicity" does not justify it.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5)
- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature". There is no fraud carve-out.
- **Buyer wants:** An express carve-out from every limitation, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provision for fraud, dishonesty or wilful concealment by the Seller, the Company or their officers, employees or advisers. Non-reliance should not purport to exclude claims under the Australian Consumer Law for misleading conduct (ss 18/236) where those arise from fraud or wilful non-disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** Non-negotiable insertion. **Reason:** As drafted, the clauses would let the Seller argue fraud is capped at AUD 4.8m and time-barred at 18 months. No buyer should accept that.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope (Schedule 7; DL 1.1–1.2)
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room (to 22 September 2026), the Accounts, the statutory registers and all publicly searchable records. DL 1.4 disclaims any admission.
- **Buyer wants:** Specific disclosure only. Each disclosure must be fair, with sufficient detail for the Buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and assess its impact, and must be referenced against specific warranties. The data room should be "disclosed" only through an agreed, attached index and USB copy, if at all. Public registers should be limited to searches the Buyer actually ran on a named date. No disclosure against fundamental warranties, tax, or matters covered by specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** Strike the general disclosure in 1.1–1.2. **Reason:** Blanket data-room disclosure moves all diligence risk to the Buyer and guts the warranties.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier (cl 8.3)
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew of, or that was "discoverable" from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer wants:** Express pro-sandbagging: Buyer knowledge, actual or constructive, does not reduce claims. The fallback is that only matters Fairly Disclosed in the Disclosure Letter qualify warranties.
- **Recommendation:** Delete, with the fallback above. **Reason:** "Discoverable" and "advisers' knowledge" are constructive-knowledge standards that would bar claims on exactly the issues diligence has flagged.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent (cl 3/6.3; DD-002)
- **Seller:** "Addressed". Seller uses reasonable endeavours, and the condition is satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. **DL 2 confirms no final consent and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are met.**
- **Buyer wants:**
  - A condition precedent requiring a final written consent from Bluefen to the change of control that is unconditional, or conditional only on terms acceptable to the Buyer.
  - Evidence that every condition in cl 11.3 of DD-002 has been satisfied.
  - Satisfaction of the condition to be confirmed by the Buyer, and waivable only by the Buyer.
  - The Seller to use best or all reasonable endeavours.
  - A long-stop date with a Buyer termination right.
  - Ideally, a price adjustment or specific indemnity if Bluefen terminates or exercises change-control rights within around 12 months.
- **Recommendation:** Treat this as a hard condition precedent. Do not sign on the Seller's formulation. **Reason:** About AUD 3.6m, roughly 30% of FY26 revenue, depends on it, and the Seller's own disclosure contradicts "addressed".

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility (cl 2/7; DD-003)
- **Seller:** About AUD 3.2m outstanding, with a release "following Completion". DL 3 confirms the facility is not repaid and no discharge has been given.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Repayment at Completion out of the purchase price as Debt, shown as a line item in the funds flow.
  - A payout letter delivered before Completion.
  - At Completion: a deed of release, PPSR (personal property securities register) financing-statement discharges and the return of any share certificates held as security, including any security over the sale shares.
  - Confirmation that the change of control clause (cl 8.1) is not triggered before payout.
- **Recommendation:** Reject a post-Completion release. Make discharge a Completion deliverable. **Reason:** This is a debt-free deal, so leaving AUD 3.2m of secured debt and a live change-control default with the Company after Completion breaches the baseline.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses (DD-005)
- **Seller:** AUD 420,000 in Completion bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. DL 5 is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.
- **Buyer wants:** The bonuses plus all on-costs (payroll tax, super guarantee, PAYG withholding, workers' compensation) treated as Transaction Expenses or Debt and deducted from the price. Alternatively, the Seller pays them and gives a specific indemnity. Either way, they must appear in the funds flow, with PAYG processed through Company payroll at Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Itemise and deduct. **Reason:** The Company is the employer and bears the liability. "A matter for the Seller" with no mechanism means the Buyer funds AUD 420k plus perhaps another 10–15% in on-costs.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity (cl 11.1; DD-004/DD-010)
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is considered adequate.
- **The problem:** Under DD-004 cl 7.3, title to the SOW3 Project Materials passes only on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee. AUD 180,000 is open, there is no bank verification and there is no confirmatory assignment (DL 4).
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Payment of all SOW3 fees before Completion, evidenced by Ironquay's written receipt.
  - An executed confirmatory IP assignment as a Completion deliverable. Failing that, a retention in escrow of at least the open amount plus a buffer.
  - A specific indemnity, outside the cap and thresholds, covering the open fees and any third-party IP claim, loss of use, re-development cost and remediation.
- **Recommendation:** Expand the indemnity. **Reason:** The risk is not the AUD 180k fee. It is that the Company may not own IP it uses, and a payment-only indemnity does not cover that.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (cl 4.6/Sch 6; DD-006)
- **Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material." DL 6 records about 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps) sent via a link to an unintended external address. Access, scope and notifiability are undetermined as at 22 September 2026.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Immediate updated information. More than 6 weeks have passed, and a notifiable data breach assessment under the Privacy Act (Part IIIC) must generally be completed within 30 days of awareness.
  - Copies of the assessment, any notification to the OAIC or individuals, link-access logs and remediation steps.
  - A pre-Completion covenant covering investigation and notification conduct, with Buyer consultation rights.
  - A specific indemnity, outside the cap, thresholds and disclosure, covering regulatory penalties, notification and remediation costs, third-party claims and customer contractual claims.
  - A carve-out of this matter from the Seller's general disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** Obtain the facts now and add a specific indemnity. **Reason:** Exposure is unquantified and potentially regulatory, and the Seller's "not material" contradicts its own statement that the facts are not established.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (DD-008/DD-011)
- **Seller:** Three renewals at AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 total) are "ordinary-course". DL 8 itself says they should be read together and does not state whether they are terminable, accrued or unavoidable.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - The renewal documents.
  - Treatment of the three as a single arrangement for materiality and de minimis purposes.
  - Confirmation of termination rights and accrual status.
  - A conduct-of-business covenant requiring Buyer consent to any further renewal.
  - If they are not genuinely ordinary course or not accrued, treatment as a price adjustment or leakage, or Seller cancellation before Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept the "ordinary-course" characterisation without evidence. **Reason:** Three linked AUD 110k items look like a split commitment that may sit below the material-contract and de minimis thresholds.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** A single regime: limitations apply to "all Claims" unless expressly stated otherwise (cl 12.3/13, 9.3/12.8/20.5).
- **Buyer wants:** Separately defined claim categories, each with its own cap and time limit:

| Category | Cap | Time limit |
|---|---|---|
| General Warranty Claims | 35–50% | 24 months |
| Fundamental Claims | 100% | 6–7 years |
| Tax Claims | 100% | 5–7 years |
| Specific Indemnity Claims | 100% / uncapped | Matter-specific |
| Covenant/Leakage/Price-adjustment claims | No cap | — |
| Fraud | No limits | — |

Limitations should apply only where a clause names its category.
- **Recommendation:** Restructure clause 12. **Reason:** This drafting choice determines whether every other negotiated protection actually works.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification (DD-012)
- **Seller:** Title is "evidenced" by the Company's share register. DL 10 concedes this is only the source the Seller relied on, and that the Buyer has not verified it.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Buyer verification against ASIC current and historical extracts, the full issue and transfer history (allotment resolutions, Forms 484), the constitution and any shareholder agreement for pre-emption rights, and PPSR searches against the Seller and the Company.
  - Confirmation that no options, convertibles or employee equity are outstanding.
  - Fundamental title warranties (see N-004).
  - At Completion: executed transfers, original certificates or lost-certificate indemnities, release of any Riverlark security over the shares, and a register update.
- **Recommendation:** Complete independent verification before signing. **Reason:** A register maintained by the Seller is self-serving evidence, and title is the whole deal.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP are "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:**
  - **Tax:** A separate tax indemnity or tax deed covering pre-Completion tax, including payroll tax and super on the DD-005 bonuses. Cap of 100%, 5–7 years, no thresholds, no disclosure. The Buyer controls tax disputes, with Seller consultation.
  - **IP:** Full ownership, non-infringement and assignment warranties covering the Ironquay materials and employee and contractor assignments. Ideally treated as "fundamental-lite" (higher cap, around 3 years), plus the Ironquay specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** Treat these as open and table them in our mark-up. **Reason:** We have not agreed them. Folding them into a AUD 4.8m, 18-month regime would leave the core asset (data/IP) and statutory tax largely unprotected.

---

### Other points to note
- **Lease (DL 7) and Mossvale (DL 9):** The Seller says these involve notification only, or no consent triggered by a share sale. We should confirm against the clause text, and add a Seller covenant to give any lease notification and a warranty that no change-of-control right exists.
- **DL 1.4 (no admissions):** This is acceptable only if it cannot dilute specific indemnities. Add language that it does not limit any indemnity or Fair Disclosure standard.
- **Data room cut-off (22 September 2026):** This is about 6 weeks old. Require a refreshed disclosure at signing and a bring-down at Completion, with the Buyer able to walk away or claim for new material matters.

**Suggested priority order for the mark-up:**
1. Fraud carve-out and category separation (N-005, N-014).
2. Fundamental and title protections (N-004, N-015).
3. Bluefen condition precedent and Riverlark payout (N-008, N-009).
4. Disclosure and knowledge qualifiers (N-006, N-007).
5. Specific indemnities for Ironquay, DD-006 and the bonuses (N-010 to N-012).
6. Commercial numbers (N-001 to N-003).
7. Sandbar and tax/IP terms (N-013, N-016).

- **Recommendation:** Itemise and deduct. **Reason:** The Company is the employer and bears the liability. "A matter for the Seller" with no mechanism means the Buyer funds AUD 420k plus perhaps another 10–15% in on-costs.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity (cl 11.1; DD-004/DD-010)
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is considered adequate.
- **The problem:** Under DD-004 cl 7.3, title to the SOW3 Project Materials passes only on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee. AUD 180,000 is open, there is no bank verification and there is no confirmatory assignment (DL 4).
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Payment of all SOW3 fees before Completion, evidenced by Ironquay's written receipt.
  - An executed confirmatory IP assignment as a Completion deliverable. Failing that, a retention in escrow of at least the open amount plus a buffer.
  - A specific indemnity, outside the cap and thresholds, covering the open fees and any third-party IP claim, loss of use, re-development cost and remediation.
- **Recommendation:** Expand the indemnity. **Reason:** The risk is not the AUD 180k fee. It is that the Company may not own IP it uses, and a payment-only indemnity does not cover that.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (cl 4.6/Sch 6; DD-006)
- **Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material." DL 6 records about 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps) sent via a link to an unintended external address. Access, scope and notifiability are undetermined as at 22 September 2026.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Immediate updated information. More than 6 weeks have passed, and a notifiable data breach assessment under the Privacy Act (Part IIIC) must generally be completed within 30 days of awareness.
  - Copies of the assessment, any notification to the OAIC or individuals, link-access logs and remediation steps.
  - A pre-Completion covenant covering investigation and notification conduct, with Buyer consultation rights.
  - A specific indemnity, outside the cap, thresholds and disclosure, covering regulatory penalties, notification and remediation costs, third-party claims and customer contractual claims.
  - A carve-out of this matter from the Seller's general disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** Obtain the facts now and add a specific indemnity. **Reason:** Exposure is unquantified and potentially regulatory, and the Seller's "not material" contradicts its own statement that the facts are not established.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (DD-008/DD-011)
- **Seller:** Three renewals at AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 total) are "ordinary-course". DL 8 itself says they should be read together and does not state whether they are terminable, accrued or unavoidable.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - The renewal documents.
  - Treatment of the three as a single arrangement for materiality and de minimis purposes.
  - Confirmation of termination rights and accrual status.
  - A conduct-of-business covenant requiring Buyer consent to any further renewal.
  - If they are not genuinely ordinary course or not accrued, treatment as a price adjustment or leakage, or Seller cancellation before Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept the "ordinary-course" characterisation without evidence. **Reason:** Three linked AUD 110k items look like a split commitment that may sit below the material-contract and de minimis thresholds.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** A single regime: limitations apply to "all Claims" unless expressly stated otherwise (cl 12.3/13, 9.3/12.8/20.5).
- **Buyer wants:** Separately defined claim categories, each with its own cap and time limit:

| Category | Cap | Time limit |
|---|---|---|
| General Warranty Claims | 35–50% | 24 months |
| Fundamental Claims | 100% | 6–7 years |
| Tax Claims | 100% | 5–7 years |
| Specific Indemnity Claims | 100% / uncapped | Matter-specific |
| Covenant/Leakage/Price-adjustment claims | No cap | — |
| Fraud | No limits | — |

Limitations should apply only where a clause names its category.
- **Recommendation:** Restructure clause 12. **Reason:** This drafting choice determines whether every other negotiated protection actually works.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification (DD-012)
- **Seller:** Title is "evidenced" by the Company's share register. DL 10 concedes this is only the source the Seller relied on, and that the Buyer has not verified it.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Buyer verification against ASIC current and historical extracts, the full issue and transfer history (allotment resolutions, Forms 484), the constitution and any shareholder agreement for pre-emption rights, and PPSR searches against the Seller and the Company.
  - Confirmation that no options, convertibles or employee equity are outstanding.
  - Fundamental title warranties (see N-004).
  - At Completion: executed transfers, original certificates or lost-certificate indemnities, release of any Riverlark security over the shares, and a register update.
- **Recommendation:** Complete independent verification before signing. **Reason:** A register maintained by the Seller is self-serving evidence, and title is the whole deal.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP are "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:**
  - **Tax:** A separate tax indemnity or tax deed covering pre-Completion tax, including payroll tax and super on the DD-005 bonuses. Cap of 100%, 5–7 years, no thresholds, no disclosure. The Buyer controls tax disputes, with Seller consultation.
  - **IP:** Full ownership, non-infringement and assignment warranties covering the Ironquay materials and employee and contractor assignments. Ideally treated as "fundamental-lite" (higher cap, around 3 years), plus the Ironquay specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** Treat these as open and table them in our mark-up. **Reason:** We have not agreed them. Folding them into a AUD 4.8m, 18-month regime would leave the core asset (data/IP) and statutory tax largely unprotected.
